## The Cosmic Microwave Background

<br/>
<br/>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="51%"}
![](PhD/1_intro/CMB/horn_antenna.jpg){fig-align="center" width="100%" style="margin: 0;"}

[1965, Holmdel: Penzias & Wilson find a 3 K signal from every direction · Credit: NASA (antenna); ESA / Planck Collaboration (map)]{.credit}
:::

::: {.column width="47%"}
:::: {style="font-size: 0.75em;"}
- The [relic light of the hot Big Bang]{.kw}, released 380 000 years after it

::: {.fragment}
- At Princeton, [Dicke, Peebles, Roll & Wilkinson]{.kw} had predicted this relic radiation and were building a radiometer to find it
- The two groups published side by side in 1965: [Penzias & Wilson]{.kw} the measurement, Princeton the interpretation
:::

::: {.fragment}
![](PhD/1_intro/CMB/cmb_map_transparent.png){fig-align="center" width="92%"}
:::
::::
:::
::::

::: {.fragment}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body}
The discovery of the [CMB]{.kw} confirmed the expanding universe
:::
::::
:::

## Primordial gravitational waves {corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg"}

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg){.corner .print-only}

:::: {.columns style="display: flex; align-items: center; min-height: 540px;"}
::: {.column width="44%"}
- Quantum fluctuations perturb the [metric]{.kw} of space-time
- [Scalar]{.kw}: $\Delta_s^2(k) = A_s\,(k/k_*)^{n_s-1}$
- [Tensor]{.kw}: $\Delta_t^2(k) = A_t\,(k/k_*)^{n_t}$, the [gravitational waves]{.kw}

:::: {.fragment}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #25406b; --eq-size: 1em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; width: fit-content; margin: 0.4em auto;"}
$$
r \equiv \frac{A_t}{A_s} \;\propto\; E_\mathrm{inf}^4
$$
:::

The tensor-to-scalar ratio fixes the [energy scale of inflation]{.kw}
::::

::: {.fragment}
Primordial GWs leave a unique imprint in the CMB [polarisation]{.kw2}
:::
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/02_primordial_gw/scalar_tensor.gif){.screen-only fig-align="center" width="100%"}

![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/02_primordial_gw/scalar_tensor_last.svg){.print-only fig-align="center" width="100%"}
:::
::::

## Polarisation of the CMB {corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg"}

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg){.corner .print-only}

:::: {.row .bare style="--gap: 0.6em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
::: {style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5em; flex: 0 0 auto;"}
[$A_s$]{.tag}

[$A_t$]{.tag}
:::

::: {style="position: relative; flex: 1 1 auto;"}
![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/03_polarisation/polarised_photon.gif){.screen-only style="display: block; width: 100%;"}

![](PhD/1_intro/CMB/cmb_map_transparent.png){.screen-only style="position: absolute; left: 66.25%; top: 17.5%; width: 32.5%; height: 65%;"}

![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/03_polarisation/polarised_photon_last.svg){.print-only}
:::
::::

::: {.fragment}
:::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
- A quadrupole at last scattering + Thomson scattering, $\propto |\hat{\epsilon}\cdot\hat{\epsilon}'|^2$ → [linear polarisation]{.kw}
- 3 [Stokes parameters]{.kw} describe linearly polarised light
::::

![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/03_polarisation/stokes_iqu.svg){fig-align="center" width="88%"}

[Adapted from: Emma Alexander, Wikimedia Commons ([Stokes params](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Emmaalexander_Stokes_params.png))]{.credit}
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body}
$Q$ and $U$ depend on the [reference frame]{.kw}: turning it by $\psi$ mixes them, $\;Q' = Q\cos 2\psi + U\sin 2\psi$
:::
::::

$C(\theta) = \langle \Delta T(\hat n_1)\,\Delta T(\hat n_2)\rangle$ over all pairs at separation $\theta$: its expansion in Legendre polynomials gives the [$C_\ell$]{.kw}

## How do we represent sky data numerically? {#healpix corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg"}

## Spherical Harmonic Transforms {#sht corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg"}

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg){.corner .print-only}

<br/><br/>

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #25406b; --eq-math-margin: 0.35em 0; grid-column: 2;"}
$$
f(\theta,\varphi) = \sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty} \sum_{m=-\ell}^{\ell} a_{\ell m}\, Y_\ell^m(\theta,\varphi)

C_\ell = \frac{1}{2\ell+1} \sum_{m=-\ell}^{\ell} |a_{\ell m}|^2
$$

## Predicted CMB power spectra {corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg"}

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg){.corner .print-only}

::: {.r-stack}

![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/09_power_spectrum/cl_step2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1 width="92%"}

![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/09_power_spectrum/cl_step3.svg){.fragment fragment-index=2 width="92%"}
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=3}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body}
- [The primordial tensor perturbations]{.kw} are a clear probe of [$r$]{.kw} and of the inflation period
- They are measurable through [$C_\ell^{BB}$]{.kw2} of the [CMB]{.kw}
- Current surveys forecast an upper bound of [$r \approx 0.003$]{.kw}
:::
::::
:::

## Current constraints on $r$ {corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg"}

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_cmb.svg){.corner .print-only}

![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/10_r_constraints/r_constraints.svg){fig-align="center" width="74%"}

::: {.fragment}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body}
- Best limit: [$r < 0.032$]{.kw} (95 %, Planck PR4 + BICEP/Keck 2018)
- The main obstacle is the [Galactic foregrounds]{.kw} that obscure the [CMB]{.kw}: [Contribution 1]{.kw2}
:::
::::
:::

::: {.column width="46%"}

::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=1 style="--eq-border: #2aa198; --eq-size: 0.8em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; --eq-pad: 0.2em 1.2em; text-align: center;"}
[redshift]{.kw style="display: block;"} $1 + z = \dfrac{\lambda_\mathrm{obs}}{\lambda_\mathrm{emit}} = \dfrac{1}{a}$
:::

::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=2 style="--eq-border: #2aa198; --eq-size: 0.8em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; --eq-pad: 0.2em 1.2em; text-align: center;"}
[scale factor]{.kw style="display: block;"} $a(t),\qquad a_0 = 1,\qquad H = \dot a / a$
:::


::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=3 style="--eq-border: #2aa198; --eq-size: 0.8em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; --eq-pad: 0.2em 1.2em; text-align: center;"}

:::

::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=4 style="--eq-border: #2aa198; --eq-size: 0.8em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; --eq-pad: 0.2em 1.2em; text-align: center;"}
[expansion rate]{.kw style="display: block;"} $H(z) = H_0\sqrt{\Omega_m(1+z)^3 + \Omega_\Lambda}$
:::

Dark energy accelerates the expansion today: it sets [$H(z)$]{.kw}, hence distances and the growth of structure

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_lss.svg){.corner .print-only}

<br/>

![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/02_lensing/weak_lensing_illustration.png){fig-align="center" width="86%"}

Matter along the line of sight bends light: [every background galaxy is slightly distorted]{.kw}

## Convergence and shear {corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_lss.svg"}

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_lss.svg){.corner .print-only}

![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/03_convergence_shear/galaxy_distortion.gif){.screen-only fig-align="center" width="70%" style="margin: 1.2em auto -0.9em;"}

![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/03_convergence_shear/galaxy_distortion_last.png){.print-only fig-align="center" width="70%" style="margin: 1.2em auto -0.9em;"}

::: {.grid style="--cols: 1fr 1fr 1fr; width: 70%; margin: 0 auto; text-align: center; font-size: 0.8em;"}
[galaxy]{}

[convergence [$\kappa$]{.kw} (spin 0)]{}

[shear [$\gamma_1, \gamma_2$]{.kw} (spin 2)]{}
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #2aa198; width: fit-content; margin: 0.3em auto 0; --eq-size: 1em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0;"}
$$
\mathbf{A} = \begin{pmatrix} 1-\kappa-\gamma_1 & -\gamma_2 \\ -\gamma_2 & 1-\kappa+\gamma_1 \end{pmatrix}
$$
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.95em;"}
Matter deforms galaxies through [weak lensing]{.kw}, by a [spin-0]{.kw2} field, the [convergence $\kappa$]{.kw}, and a [spin-2]{.kw2} field, the two components of the [shear $\gamma$]{.kw}

::: {.fragment}
[Fun fact]{.kw2}: [$\kappa$, $\gamma$]{.kw2} relate like [$Q$, $U$]{.kw2}: $\gamma_1 + i\gamma_2$ is the same mathematical object as $Q + iU$, and splits into [$E$ and $B$]{.kw2} modes in the same way
:::
:::
::::
:::

## Kaiser–Squires on the sphere {corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_lss.svg"}

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_lss.svg){.corner .print-only}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column style="width: 45%; padding-top: 1em;"}
[From $\kappa$ to $\gamma$]{.kw}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #2aa198; --eq-size: 0.8em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0;"}
$$
\gamma^E_{\ell m} = -\sqrt{\frac{(\ell+2)(\ell-1)}{\ell(\ell+1)}}\;\kappa_{\ell m}, \qquad \gamma^B_{\ell m} = 0
$$
$$
\gamma_1 + i\gamma_2 = \sum_{\ell m} \gamma^E_{\ell m}\;{}_2Y_{\ell m}
$$
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
[From $\gamma$ back to $\kappa$]{.kw}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #2aa198; --eq-size: 0.8em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0;"}
$$
\kappa_{\ell m} = -\sqrt{\frac{\ell(\ell+1)}{(\ell+2)(\ell-1)}}\;\gamma^E_{\ell m}
$$
:::
:::
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
:::: {.cell .bare style="--img-w: 200px; --cap-size: 0.6em; --cell-margin: 0.1em 0 0;"}
![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/04_kaiser_squires/kappa.gif){.screen-only}
![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/04_kaiser_squires/kappa.png){.print-only}

[convergence κ]{.caption}
::::

::: {style="text-align: center; margin: 0.1em 0; line-height: 0;"}
[]{.arrow .down style="--len: 34px; --head: 20px;"}
:::

:::: {.row .bare style="--gap: 24px; --justify: center; --img-w: 175px; --cap-size: 0.6em; --cell-margin: 0.1em 0 0;"}
::: {.cell}
![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/04_kaiser_squires/gamma1.gif){.screen-only}
![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/04_kaiser_squires/gamma1.png){.print-only}

[shear γ~1~]{.caption}
:::

::: {.cell}
![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/04_kaiser_squires/gamma2.gif){.screen-only}
![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/04_kaiser_squires/gamma2.png){.print-only}

[shear γ~2~]{.caption}
:::
::::
:::
::::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.75em;"}
- Kaiser–Squires is a [simple per-$\ell$ rescaling]{.kw} between $\kappa$ and the $E$-mode of the shear: one field, two views

:::
::::
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=6}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.75em;"}
- Each source bin sees the [integral of all the matter]{.kw} in front of it: $\kappa_i(\hat n) = \int_0^{\chi_i} q_i(\chi)\,\delta(\chi\hat n,\chi)\,\mathrm{d}\chi$
- Farther bins cross more matter and see a stronger $\kappa$; comparing bins follows the [growth of structure]{.kw2} along the line of sight
:::
::::
:::

## The two-point analysis {corner="PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_lss.svg"}

<br/>
<br/>

![](PhD/1_intro/lcdm/lcdm_model_lss.svg){.corner .print-only}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/07_matter_spectrum/pk_lin_nl.svg){fig-align="center" width="100%"}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #2aa198; --eq-size: 0.8em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; margin-top: 1.6em;"}
$$
C_\ell^{ij} = \int \mathrm{d}\chi\, \frac{q_i(\chi)\,q_j(\chi)}{\chi^2}\; P\!\left(k=\tfrac{\ell+1/2}{\chi}, z\right)
$$
:::

[Each multipole $\ell$ reads the [matter spectrum]{.kw} at $k = \ell/\chi$, weighted by the [lensing kernels $q_i$]{.kw2} of the tomographic bins]{style="font-size: 0.8em;"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
![](PhD/3_observation/weaklensing/07_matter_spectrum/cl_kappa.svg){fig-align="center" width="100%" style="margin: 0.2em 0 0;"}
:::
:::
::::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
- [$\Omega_\mathrm{m}$]{.kw}: how much matter · [$\sigma_8$]{.kw}: how clumpy it is on $8\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$ scales
- Weak lensing probes both parameters, and best the combination [$S_8 = \sigma_8\sqrt{\Omega_\mathrm{m}/0.3}$]{.kw2}
:::
::::
:::

# Statistical inference for cosmology

::: {.rail-stack}
![](PhD/2_outline/rail_full.svg){.rail-full}

![](PhD/2_outline/rail_focus_stats.svg){.rail-focus}
:::

## Inverse problems in cosmology

![](PhD/4_inference/01_inverse_problem/inverse_problem.svg){fig-align="center" width="80%"}


## Solving Inverse Problems : Analytical likelihood

<br/>

[Analytical inversion]{.kw} [(Stompor et al. 2009)]{style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #6E6E6E;"}

::: {.grid style="--cols: auto 1fr; --gap: 1.2em; --row-gap: 1.05em; --align: center; margin-top: 0.8em; font-size: 0.9em;"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-size: 1.3em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 1em; justify-self: stretch; text-align: center;"}
$$\mathbf{d} = \mathbf{A}(\boldsymbol\theta)\,\mathbf{s} + \mathbf{n}$$
:::

the data are linear in the signal $\mathbf{s}$, and the mixing $\mathbf{A}$ depends on a few parameters $\boldsymbol\theta$

::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=1 style="--eq-size: 1.3em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 1em; justify-self: stretch; text-align: center;"}
$$-2\ln\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol\theta,\mathbf{s}) = \big(\mathbf{d}-\mathbf{A}\mathbf{s}\big)^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\big(\mathbf{d}-\mathbf{A}\mathbf{s}\big)$$
:::

[for Gaussian noise of covariance $\mathbf{N}$]{.fragment fragment-index=1}

::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=2 style="--eq-size: 1.3em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 1em; justify-self: stretch; text-align: center;"}
$$\hat{\mathbf{s}}(\boldsymbol\theta) = \left(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\mathbf{A}\right)^{-1}\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\mathbf{d}$$
:::

[setting the derivative with respect to $\mathbf{s}$ to zero]{.fragment fragment-index=2}

::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=3 style="--eq-size: 1.3em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 1em; justify-self: stretch; text-align: center;"}
$$-2\ln\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol\theta) = -\left(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\mathbf{d}\right)^{\top}\left(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\mathbf{A}\right)^{-1}\left(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\mathbf{d}\right)$$
:::

[substituting $\hat{\mathbf{s}}$ back, up to a constant, leaves a likelihood of $\boldsymbol\theta$ alone]{.fragment fragment-index=3}
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=4}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 1.2em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
- The signal $\mathbf{s}$ is removed analytically, so only the few parameters $\boldsymbol\theta$ are searched
- This requires a model [linear in $\mathbf{s}$]{.kw} with Gaussian noise
:::
::::
:::

## Solving Inverse Problems : Forward Modelling {visibility="uncounted"}

<br/>

[Forward modelling]{.kw}


::: {.grid style="--cols: 1fr 1fr 1.15fr; --gap: 1em; --align: start;"}
::: {.fragment fragment-index=1 style="text-align: center;"}
[Implicit inference]{.kw2}

![](PhD/4_inference/02_forward_modelling/implicit.svg){height="500px" style="margin: 0.2em auto 0;"}
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2 style="text-align: center;"}
[Explicit inference]{.kw}

![](PhD/4_inference/02_forward_modelling/explicit.svg){height="500px" style="margin: 0.2em auto 0;"}
:::

::: {style="padding-top: 1.6em;"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-size: 0.95em; --eq-math-margin: 0.15em 0; --eq-pad: 0.3em 0.8em; margin: 0 0 0.6em; text-align: center;"}
$$\hat{\mathbf{d}} = \mathcal{A}(\mathbf{s},\boldsymbol\theta)$$
:::

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-size: 0.95em; --eq-math-margin: 0.15em 0; --eq-pad: 0.3em 0.8em; margin: 0 0 1em; text-align: center;"}
$$-\ln\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol\theta,\mathbf{s}) \;\propto\; \frac{\lVert \hat{\mathbf{d}} - \mathbf{d} \rVert_2^2}{\sigma^2}$$
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=3}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
- Explicit inference is more [interpretable]{.kw} than its implicit counterpart
- It fits the latent field [$\mathbf{s}$]{.kw} together with $\boldsymbol\theta$, instead of marginalising over it
:::
::::
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=4}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 1em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
This thesis uses explicit inference for both the [analytical model]{.kw2} and the [forward model]{.kw2}
:::
::::
:::
:::
:::

## Bayesian inference in cosmology

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column style="width: 60%;"}
[Bayes' theorem]{.kw}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-math-margin: 0.25em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 1.1em; width: fit-content; margin: 0; --eq-size: 1.4em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
$$\underbrace{p(\boldsymbol\theta\mid\mathbf{d})}_{\text{posterior}} \;=\; \frac{\overbrace{p(\mathbf{d}\mid\boldsymbol\theta)}^{\text{likelihood}}\;\overbrace{p(\boldsymbol\theta)}^{\text{prior}}}{\underbrace{p(\mathbf{d})}_{\text{evidence}}}$$
:::

::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=1 style="--eq-math-margin: 0.25em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 1.1em; width: fit-content; margin: 0; --eq-size: 1.35em; margin-top: 0.8em;"}
$$p(\boldsymbol\theta\mid\mathbf{d}) \;\propto\; p(\mathbf{d}\mid\boldsymbol\theta)\;p(\boldsymbol\theta)$$
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2 style="margin-top: 1.4em;"}
[Joint probabilistic modelling]{.kw2}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-math-margin: 0.25em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 1.1em; width: fit-content; margin: 0; --eq-size: 1.3em; --eq-border: #521463; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
$$p(\boldsymbol\theta,\mathbf{s}\mid\mathbf{d}) \;\propto\; \underbrace{p(\mathbf{d}\mid\mathbf{s},\boldsymbol\theta)}_{\text{likelihood}}\;\underbrace{p(\mathbf{s}\mid\boldsymbol\theta)}_{\text{latent prior}}\;\underbrace{p(\boldsymbol\theta)}_{\text{prior}}$$
:::
:::
:::

::: {.column style="width: 40%;"}
![](PhD/4_inference/03_bayesian_inference/bayes_posterior.svg){width="100%" style="margin: 0;"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
![](PhD/4_inference/03_bayesian_inference/hierarchical_model.svg){height="115px" style="display: block; margin: 3.2em auto 0;"}
:::
:::
::::

## Optimising the posterior

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column style="width: 50%; text-align: center;"}
[Minimising the negative log-likelihood]{.kw}

::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=3}
![](PhD/4_inference/04_optimising_posterior/minimise.gif){.screen-only height="360px" style="margin: 0.2em 0 0;"}
![](PhD/4_inference/04_optimising_posterior/minimise.png){.print-only height="360px" style="margin: 0.2em 0 0;"}
:::

![](PhD/4_inference/04_optimising_posterior/laplace.svg){.fragment fragment-index=3 height="360px" style="margin: 0.2em 0 0;"}
:::
:::

::: {.column .fragment fragment-index=1 style="width: 50%; text-align: center;"}
[Sampling the full posterior]{.kw}

::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=3}
![](PhD/4_inference/04_optimising_posterior/sample.gif){.screen-only height="360px" style="margin: 0.2em 0 0;"}
![](PhD/4_inference/04_optimising_posterior/sample.png){.print-only height="360px" style="margin: 0.2em 0 0;"}
:::

![](PhD/4_inference/04_optimising_posterior/hpd.svg){.fragment fragment-index=4 height="360px" style="margin: 0.2em 0 0;"}
:::
:::
::::

::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 style="width: 100%;"}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="text-align: center; font-size: 1.05em;"}
How do we measure how much we [trust the result]{.kw}?
:::
::::
:::

::: {.grid style="--cols: 1fr 1fr; --gap: 1.2em; --align: stretch; width: 100%;"}
::: {.fragment fragment-index=3}
:::: {.solutionbox style="height: 100%;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.9em;"}
The inverse Hessian of $-\ln\mathcal{L}$ at the minimum gives the covariance, $\mathbf{C} = \mathbf{H}^{-1}$, and with it the [confidence intervals]{.kw}, assuming the posterior is Gaussian
:::
::::
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=4}
:::: {.solutionbox style="height: 100%;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.9em;"}
The samples give the [credible regions]{.kw} directly: the smallest regions holding 68, 95 and 99.7 % of them
:::
::::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=5 style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; min-height: 700px; z-index: 20; background: rgba(250, 247, 240, 0.86); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center;"}
:::: {.solutionbox style="width: 88%;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="text-align: center; font-size: 1.15em;"}
Both methods become more efficient with a [differentiable likelihood]{.kw}
:::
::::
:::

## Differentiable programming

<br/>
<br/>

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column style="width: 38%; text-align: center;"}
![](assets/Logos/JaxLogo.png){style="display: block; height: 95px; margin: 0 auto 22px;"}
![](assets/optax_logo.svg){style="display: block; height: 95px; margin: 0 auto 22px;"}
![](assets/Logos/blackjax_icon.png){style="display: block; height: 95px; margin: 0 auto 22px;"}
![](assets/Logos/numpyro_transparent.png){style="display: block; height: 95px; margin: 0 auto;"}
:::

::: {.column width="62%"}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 0.6em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 1.2em;"}
- [JAX]{.kw} computes exact gradients of numerical code by automatic differentiation
- Custom gradients replace the automatic ones where memory or speed requires it
- The same code runs on CPUs, GPUs and multi-GPU clusters
- I used [Optax]{.kw2} for optimisation
- [BlackJAX]{.kw2} and [NumPyro]{.kw2} for sampling
:::
::::
:::
::::

::: {.fragment}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="text-align: center;"}
Can better numerical methods extract [more cosmology]{.kw} from the same data?
:::
::::
:::

## Parametric component separation: the spectral model

<br/>

### [Synchrotron and dust (Galactic foregrounds)]{.kw}

:::: {.columns style="text-align: center;"}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #3b6fb6; --eq-size: 1.05em; --eq-math-margin: 0.1em 0 0.2em; --eq-pad: 0.25em 0.9em 0.05em; width: fit-content; margin: 0.2em auto 0.3em;"}
[[Synchrotron]{style="color: #3b6fb6; font-weight: 700;"}: power law]{style="font-size: 0.75em;"}

$$A^{\mathrm{sync}}_\nu({\color{#3b6fb6}\beta_s}) \;\propto\; \left(\frac{\nu}{\nu_0}\right)^{\color{#3b6fb6}\beta_s}$$
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/02_spectral_model/planck_sync.png){height="165px" style="margin: 0;"}

[Planck: synchrotron]{style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #6E6E6E; display: block; margin-top: -0.9em;"}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #d68910; --eq-size: 1.05em; --eq-math-margin: 0.1em 0 0.2em; --eq-pad: 0.25em 0.9em 0.05em; width: fit-content; margin: 0.2em auto 0.3em;"}
[[Dust]{style="color: #d68910; font-weight: 700;"}: modified black body]{style="font-size: 0.75em;"}

$$A^{\mathrm{dust}}_\nu({\color{#d68910}\beta_d}, {\color{#d68910}T_d}) \;\propto\; \left(\frac{\nu}{\nu_0}\right)^{{\color{#d68910}\beta_d}+1}\frac{e^{h\nu_0/k{\color{#d68910}T_d}}-1}{e^{h\nu/k{\color{#d68910}T_d}}-1}$$
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/02_spectral_model/planck_dust.png){height="165px" style="margin: 0;"}

[Planck: thermal dust]{style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #6E6E6E; display: block; margin-top: -0.9em;"}
:::
::::

::: {.fragment}
### [The spectral likelihood]{.kw}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #521463; --eq-size: 1.1em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; width: fit-content; margin: 0.3em auto 0; text-align: center;"}
$$\mathbf{d}_\nu = A^{\mathrm{cmb}}_\nu\,\mathbf{s}_{\mathrm{cmb}} + A^{\mathrm{dust}}_\nu({\color{#d68910}\beta_d},{\color{#d68910}T_d})\,\mathbf{s}_{\mathrm{dust}} + A^{\mathrm{sync}}_\nu({\color{#3b6fb6}\beta_s})\,\mathbf{s}_{\mathrm{sync}} + \mathbf{n}_\nu$$
:::
:::

<br/>

::: {.fragment}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #521463; --eq-size: 1.1em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; width: fit-content; margin: 0.45em auto 0; text-align: center;"}
$$-2\ln\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol\beta) = -\left(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\mathbf{d}\right)^{\top}\left(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\mathbf{A}\right)^{-1}\left(\mathbf{A}^{\top}\mathbf{N}^{-1}\mathbf{d}\right), \qquad \boldsymbol\beta = ({\color{#d68910}\beta_d}, {\color{#d68910}T_d}, {\color{#3b6fb6}\beta_s})$$
:::
:::

- The number of patches must be tuned to meet the requirements of future surveys

## Fast and robust minimisation

::::::: {.columns style="display: flex; gap: 12px; margin-top: 0.1em;"}
:::::: {.column style="width: 480px;"}
::::: {.r-stack .bare}
:::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 style="margin: 40px 0 0 20px; align-self: start; justify-self: start;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/06_newton/newton_bowl.gif){.screen-only style="width: 450px;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/06_newton/newton_bowl.png){.print-only style="width: 450px;"}
::::

:::: {.fragment fragment-index=2 style="margin: 0 0 0 40px; align-self: start; justify-self: start;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/06_newton/noise_left.gif){.screen-only style="width: 430px;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/06_newton/noise_left.png){.print-only style="width: 430px;"}
::::
:::::
::::::

:::::: {.column style="width: 500px;"}
### How do we minimise? {style="margin: 0 0 0.3em;"}

::::: {.r-stack .bare style="height: 300px;"}
:::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1 style="width: 100%;"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-size: 1.25em; --eq-math-margin: 0.25em 0; --eq-pad: 0.3em 0.9em; width: fit-content; margin: 0.4em auto 0; text-align: center;"}
[The Newton method]{style="display: block; margin: 0.1em 0 0; font-size: 0.8em; font-weight: 700; color: #C2560A;"}

$$\boldsymbol\beta_{k+1} = \boldsymbol\beta_k - \mathbf{H}_k^{-1}\,\mathbf{g}_k$$
$$\mathbf{g} = \nabla_{\boldsymbol\beta}\left(-\ln\mathcal{L}\right), \qquad \mathbf{H} = \nabla^2_{\boldsymbol\beta}\left(-\ln\mathcal{L}\right)$$
:::
::::

:::: {.fragment fragment-index=1 style="width: 100%; text-align: center;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/06_newton/snr_map.png){style="width: 440px; margin: 0.2em 0 0;"}

[140 GHz, LiteBIRD depth]{style="display: block; font-size: 0.6em; color: #6E6E6E; margin: 0.1em 0 0;"}
::::
:::::

::::: {.fragment fragment-index=3 style="margin-top: 0.7em;"}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
- Noisy sky data make the Hessian [poorly conditioned]{.kw} and hard to invert
- [Quasi-Newton]{.kw} methods suffer most. They approximate the inverse Hessian as if the likelihood were a clean quadratic bowl
:::
::::
:::::
::::::
:::::::

## Adaptive moment-based methods

::: {style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 18px; margin-top: -0.2em;"}
![](assets/Logos/JaxLogo.png){style="height: 40px; margin: 0;"}
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-cadre-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/CMBSciPol/CADRE)
:::

:::: {.columns style="display: flex; align-items: center;"}
::: {.column style="width: 54%;"}
::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1}
![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/07_adam/adam_path.gif){.screen-only width="80%" style="margin: 0 auto; display: block;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/07_adam/adam_path.png){.print-only width="80%" style="margin: 0 auto; display: block;"}
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/07_adam/adabelief.svg){.fragment fragment-index=1 width="80%" style="margin: 0 auto; display: block;"}
:::
:::

::: {.column style="width: 46%; font-size: 1em;"}
[Adam]{.kw2} is the standard optimiser of machine learning, built for very many parameters and very noisy gradients

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-size: 0.95em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 0.8em; width: fit-content; margin: 0.4em auto;"}
$$\boldsymbol\beta_{t+1} = \boldsymbol\beta_t - \eta\,\frac{\hat m_t}{\sqrt{\hat v_t}+\epsilon}$$
:::

[$m_t$, $v_t$: running means of $\mathbf{g}$ and $\mathbf{g}^2$]{style="font-size: 0.85em; color: #6E6E6E;"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
[AdaBelief]{.kw2} scales the step by the spread of the gradient instead

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-size: 0.95em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; --eq-pad: 0.15em 0.8em; width: fit-content; margin: 0.4em auto;"}
$$v_t \;\longrightarrow\; s_t:\ \text{running mean of }(\mathbf{g} - m_t)^2$$
:::

A noisy direction gets a [smaller step]{.kw}
:::
:::
::::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.9em;"}
[AdaTopK]{.kw} builds on AdaBelief for physical parameters, with a robust handling of parameter bounds
:::
::::
:::

## Scaling of AdaTopK

![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/08_scaling/runtime_scaling.svg){fig-align="center" width="62%" style="margin-bottom: 0.2em;"}

::: {.fragment}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-header}
Scaling
:::

::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
- AdaTopK runs on GPUs with first-order gradients only: its cost stays flat as the number of patches grows, [about 60 times faster]{.kw} than the reference solver at 10 000 patches
- Next: [scan many patch configurations]{.kw2} and select the best
:::
::::
:::

## Selection criteria for optimal patches

![](PhD/6_ending/software/logo_furax.png){style="position: absolute; top: -12px; right: 0; height: 78px; margin: 0; border-radius: 10px;"}

::: {style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 18px; margin-top: -0.2em;"}
![](assets/Logos/JaxLogo.png){style="height: 40px; margin: 0;"}
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-furax-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/CMBSciPol/furax)
[![](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-furax--cs-blue?logo=github)](https://github.com/CMBSciPol/furax-cs)
:::

<video src="PhD/5_contribution/compsep/09_selection/selection.mp4" data-autoplay muted playsinline preload="auto" style="display: block; width: 80%; margin: 0.2em auto 0;"></video>

![](PhD/5_contribution/compsep/09_selection/selection_last.png){.print-only fig-align="center" width="80%"}

::: {.fragment}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 0.3em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
- Minimising $\hat r + \sigma(r)$ cannot remove a primordial $r$. The mixing matrix $\mathbf{A}$ contains the CMB with its known spectrum, so the recovered CMB keeps [unit response]{.kw} for every partition
- The guarantee is specific to map-based parametric separation. A forward model or a non-map-based method loses it
:::
::::
:::

## Building a survey-level differentiable forward model

:::: {.hl-host .bare style="margin-top: 0.1em;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/01_pipeline/pipeline.svg){width="800px" style="display: block;"}

::: {.hlbox style="--x: 22%; --y: 5%; --w: 42%; --h: 42%;"}
:::
::::

::: {.fragment}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body}
A [fast]{.kw} and [differentiable]{.kw} gravity solver that can simulate [Stage IV survey volumes]{.kw}
:::
::::
:::

## The gravity solver: Lagrangian perturbation theory

<br/>
<br/>

::::: {.columns style="display: flex; align-items: flex-start; margin-top: 1.2em;"}
:::: {.column style="width: 42%;"}
[Each particle moves from its initial grid position $\mathbf{q}$]{style="font-size: 0.85em;"}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-size: 0.8em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; --eq-pad: 0.2em 0.6em; width: fit-content; margin: 0.4em auto;"}
$$\mathbf{x}(\mathbf{q}, a) = \mathbf{q} + D_1(a)\,\mathbf{\Psi}^{(1)}(\mathbf{q}) + D_2(a)\,\mathbf{\Psi}^{(2)}(\mathbf{q}) + \dots$$
$$\nabla \cdot \mathbf{\Psi}^{(1)} = -\delta_\mathrm{ini}$$
:::

[First order: the Zel'dovich approximation. Second order (2LPT) adds the tidal field.]{style="font-size: 0.8em; color: #6E6E6E;"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 0.9em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
- Perturbation theory does not capture the [non-linear]{.kw style="white-space: nowrap;"} growth of structure
- We need a [fast]{.kw} and [differentiable]{.kw} gravity solver that can model the [non-linear]{.kw style="white-space: nowrap;"} signal
:::
::::
:::
::::

:::: {.column .fragment fragment-index=1 style="width: 58%;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/04_lpt/limber_lin_vs_halofit.svg){width="100%" style="margin: 0;"}

[Lensing $C_\ell$ of the four DES Y3 bins, linear theory against halofit]{style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #6E6E6E;"}
::::
:::::

## Accuracy of the particle mesh

::: {.r-stack}
![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/06_accuracy/pm3d_frag_1.png){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1 width="1000px"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/06_accuracy/pm3d_frag_2.png){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1 width="1000px"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/06_accuracy/pm3d_frag_3.png){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 width="1000px"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/06_accuracy/pm3d_frag_4.png){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 width="1000px"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/06_accuracy/pm3d_frag_5.png){.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=4 width="1000px"}
:::

::: {.fragment}
:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
- The accuracy of a particle-mesh simulation is limited by the [resolution of its mesh]{.kw}
- At survey volume, a mesh with that resolution [does not fit on one GPU]{.kw}
- We need a [scalable]{.kw} gravity solver
:::
::::
:::

[evolved particles]{.caption style="--cap-size: 0.55em;"}

::: {.cell style="width: 250px;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/10_painting/density_shell.png)

[one HEALPix shell]{.caption style="--cap-size: 0.55em;"}

::::: {.column style="width: 50%;"}
:::: {.eqbox .fragment fragment-index=2 style="--eq-size: 0.95em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; --eq-pad: 0.2em 0.9em; width: fit-content; margin: 0 auto; text-align: center;"}
$$r = \lVert \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_o \rVert, \qquad \theta = \arccos\frac{z - z_o}{r}$$
$$\varphi = \operatorname{atan2}(y - y_o,\, x - x_o)$$
$$p = \texttt{ang2pix}(N_\mathrm{side}, \theta, \varphi)$$
::::

:::: {.fragment fragment-index=3 style="margin-top: 1.4em;"}
::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-header}
[ang2pix]{style="font-family: monospace;"}: jax-healpy
:::

::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
Implemented in jax-healpy by Pierre Chanial. 
Works by binning each particle into one pixel but it is [not differentiable]{.kw} because the pixel index is piecewise constant in the particle position, so its gradient is zero
:::
:::

:::::

#### [Bilinear interpolation]{.kw2} {style="margin: 0.2em 0;"}

:::: {.solutionbox style="text-align: left;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
Four pixels, weighted by the position between their centres: `get_interp_weights`, implemented in jax-healpy
:::
::::

::: {.column .fragment fragment-index=1 style="width: 50%; text-align: center;"}
#### [Radial basis function interpolation]{.kw} {style="margin: 0.2em 0;"}

::: {.r-stack}

:::: {.solutionbox style="text-align: left;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
The pixel and its eight neighbours (`get_all_neighbours`, implemented in jax-healpy), weighted by a Gaussian kernel of adjustable width
:::

The RBF scheme keeps the gradient and gives [control over the smoothing]{.kw}

```{=html}
<div style="position: relative; height: 0;">
```

::: {.fragment fragment-index=3 style="text-align: center; margin-top: -0.4em;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/11_lightcone/lightcone_shells.png){style="height: 440px;"}
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=4}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: -0.2em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
The 3D density field is projected onto concentric spherical shells around the observer, each at its own redshift. How should these redshifts be chosen?
:::
::::
:::

## Choosing an optimal shell spacing

:::: {.grid .bare style="--cols: 225px 1fr; --gap: 10px; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
::: {style="text-align: center;"}
[Uniform in scale factor]{.kw style="font-size: 0.75em;"}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #25406b; --eq-size: 0.72em; --eq-math-margin: 0.25em 0; --eq-pad: 0.05em 0.5em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
$$a_i = a_{\min} + \tfrac{i}{n}\,(1 - a_{\min})$$
:::
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/12_spacing/spacing_a.svg){width="800px"}
::::

:::: {.grid .bare .fragment fragment-index=1 style="--cols: 225px 1fr; --gap: 10px; margin-top: 0.2em;"}
::: {style="text-align: center;"}
[Equal volume]{.kw style="font-size: 0.75em;"}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #25406b; --eq-size: 0.72em; --eq-math-margin: 0.25em 0; --eq-pad: 0.05em 0.5em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
$$r_i^3 = r_{\min}^3 + \tfrac{i}{n}\,(r_{\max}^3 - r_{\min}^3)$$
:::

[outer shells floored at 50 Mpc/$h$]{.caption style="--cap-size: 0.55em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/12_spacing/spacing_equal_vol.svg){width="800px"}
::::

::::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 0.2em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-header style="font-size: 0.75em;"}
Equal volume spacing vs linear in scale factor spacing
:::

::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.7em;"}
Uniform steps in $a$: the innermost shell holds [three orders of magnitude]{.kw2} fewer particles than with equal volume, so it is [shot noise]{.kw} dominated

The downside of equal volume: [fewer shells]{.kw} cover the lensing kernel of the [first redshift bin]{.kw}

[Bin 1]{.kw2} is therefore not used for inference
:::
::::
:::::

## Impact of the number of shells on the accuracy {visibility="uncounted"}

::: {.grid .bare style="--cols: 150px 1fr; --gap: 10px; margin-top: 0.1em;"}
[uniform in $a$<br/>innermost shell]{.kw style="font-size: 0.7em; text-align: right;"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/13_nshells/nshells_density.svg){width="800px"}
:::

::: {.grid .bare .fragment fragment-index=1 style="--cols: 150px 1fr; --gap: 10px; margin-top: 0.1em;"}
[equal volume, drifted<br/>convergence vs Limber]{.kw style="font-size: 0.7em; text-align: right;"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/13_nshells/nshells_kappa.svg){width="800px"}
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 0.2em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-header style="font-size: 0.75em;"}
How many shells?
:::

::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.7em;"}
[More shells]{.kw}: each shell is thinner, so the innermost one holds fewer particles and is [shot-noise]{.kw} dominated

[Fewer shells]{.kw}: a few wide shells sample the lensing kernel of the first bin, so its convergence is [biased]{.kw} low below $\ell =$ [100]{.kw2}

For this work we adopt [20]{.kw2} shells
:::
::::
:::

:::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
::: {.grid .bare style="--cols: 400px 1fr; --gap: 16px; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
::: {style="text-align: center;"}
[Born approximation: straight lines of sight]{.kw style="display: block; font-size: 0.72em; margin-bottom: 0.4em;"}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #25406b; --eq-size: 0.72em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; margin: 0 auto; width: fit-content;"}
$$\kappa(\hat{\mathbf n};\chi_s) = \frac{3}{2}\,\Omega_m\Big(\frac{H_0}{c}\Big)^2 \sum_j W_j(\chi_s)\,\delta_j(\hat{\mathbf n})$$

$$W_j(\chi_s) = \int_{\mathrm{shell}\ j} \mathrm{d}\chi\;\chi\,(1+z)\Big(1-\frac{\chi}{\chi_s}\Big)$$
:::
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/19_born/born_weights.svg){width="560px"}
:::
::::

:::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
::: {.grid .bare style="--cols: 300px 1fr; --gap: 16px; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #25406b; --eq-size: 0.72em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; margin: 0 auto; width: fit-content;"}
$$\kappa_i(\hat{\mathbf n}) = \int \mathrm{d}z\; n_i(z)\,\kappa\big(\hat{\mathbf n};\chi_s(z)\big)$$
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/19_born/born_kappa.png){width="745px"}
:::
::::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=3}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 0.3em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
The Born approximation computes the convergence along [undeflected light rays]{.kw}

Post-Born ray tracing deflects them by under [1 arcmin]{.kw2}, below the accuracy of our [gravity solver]{.kw}
:::
::::
:::

# Using the forward model for field-level inference {.stack-top}

::: {.r-stack .bare style="width: 960px; margin-left: 30px; margin-top: -170px;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/02_forward_model/fm_forward.svg){width="960px"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/02_forward_model/fm_explicit.svg){width="960px"}
:::

[A first step before sampling: the initial field that [maximises the posterior]{.kw}, at fixed cosmology.]{style="display: block; margin-top: 0.8em;"}

## Field-level likelihood and scale cut

::::: {.row .bare style="--gap: 40px; --align: flex-start; --justify: center; margin-top: 0.8em;"}
:::: {style="flex: none; text-align: center;"}
[Gaussian likelihood on the convergence pixels]{.kw style="display: block; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.3em;"}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #3b6fb6; --eq-size: 1.1em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; --eq-pad: 0.2em 0.9em; width: fit-content; margin: 0 auto;"}
$$-\ln\mathcal{L}(\boldsymbol\theta,\mathbf{s}) = \sum_i \frac{\lVert \color{#c2560a}{\hat{\mathbf{d}}_i} - \mathbf{d}_i \rVert_2^2}{2\,\color{#3b6fb6}{\sigma_i^2}}$$
:::
::::

:::: {.fragment fragment-index=1 style="flex: none; width: 470px; text-align: center;"}
[Noise per pixel]{.kw style="display: block; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.3em;"}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #3b6fb6; --eq-size: 1.1em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; --eq-pad: 0.2em 0.9em; width: fit-content; margin: 0 auto;"}
$$\color{#3b6fb6}{\sigma_i} = \frac{\sigma_e}{\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{gal},i}\;\Omega_\mathrm{pix}}}$$
:::

[$\sigma_e$ shape noise per component, $n_{\mathrm{gal},i}$ galaxies per arcmin² in bin $i$, $\Omega_\mathrm{pix}$ pixel area in arcmin² at $N_\mathrm{side} = 256$]{.caption style="--cap-size: 0.55em; margin-top: 0.4em;"}

::: {.table-full style="font-size: 0.68em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
| DES Y3 | bin 1 | [bin 2]{.kw} | [bin 3]{.kw} | bin 4 |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| $n_\mathrm{gal}$ [arcmin$^{-2}$] | 1.476 | 1.479 | 1.484 | 1.461 |
| $\sigma_e$ | 0.26 | 0.26 | 0.26 | 0.26 |
:::
::::
:::::

::::: {.fragment fragment-index=2 style="margin-top: 1.8em;"}
:::: {.row .bare style="--gap: 16px; --justify: center;"}
[A [map-level scale cut]{.kw} on the prediction]{style="font-size: 0.85em;"}

::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #3b6fb6; --eq-size: 0.95em; --eq-math-margin: 0.15em 0; --eq-pad: 0.05em 0.7em; width: fit-content; margin: 0;"}
$$\color{#c2560a}{\hat{\mathbf{d}}_i} = T_\ell\big[\kappa_i(\mathbf{s},\boldsymbol\theta)\big]$$
:::
::::

:::: {.grid .bare style="--cols: 275px 54px 160px 54px 160px 54px 275px; --gap: 0; --align: center; justify-content: center; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/backup/scalecut_map.png){width="275px"}

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
[map2alm]{.kw style="display: block; font-size: 0.6em;"}

![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/08_sht/sht_arrow.svg){width="46px" style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;"}
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/backup/scalecut_alm.png){width="160px"}

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
[× $T_\ell$]{.kw style="display: block; font-size: 0.6em;"}

![](PhD/3_observation/cmb/08_sht/sht_arrow.svg){width="46px" style="display: block; margin: 0 auto;"}
:::

## Recovering the maximum a posteriori

::: {.absolute top=6 right=0 style="font-size: 0.6em; text-align: right; line-height: 1.3;"}
[Preliminary]{.kw}<br/>DES Y3 noise, $416^3$ mesh, 2LPT
:::

::::: {.r-stack .bare style="margin-top: 0.1em;"}
:::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 style="width: 100%; text-align: center;"}
::: {.r-stack}
![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/18_map/map_first.png){width="1000px"}

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
<video src="PhD/5_contribution/fli/18_map/map_run.mp4" class="screen-only" muted playsinline preload="auto" style="width: 1000px;"></video>

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/18_map/map_last.png){.print-only width="1000px"}
:::
:::
::::

:::: {.fragment fragment-index=2 style="width: 100%; text-align: center;"}
<video src="PhD/5_contribution/fli/18_map/compare_run.mp4" class="screen-only" muted playsinline preload="auto" style="width: 1000px;"></video>

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/18_map/compare_last.png){.print-only width="1000px"}
::::
:::::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=3}
:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 0.2em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.72em;"}
The reconstruction reaches the coherence of the joint Wiener filter, the best linear reconstruction from the same maps, in both bins (0.71 and 0.73 up to $\ell = 164$). Its starlet $\ell_1$ norm recovers 86 to 95 % of the truth's at scales 2 to 5, and 73 % at the finest.
:::
::::
:::

## Contribution 2: conclusion and perspectives {.frosted background-image="PhD/0_cover/bg_cosmic_web.jpg" background-size="cover" hide-chrome="true"}

:::: {.solutionbox}
::: {.solutionbox-body}
- The first differentiable weak-lensing forward model covering [a full survey footprint on the curved sky]{.kw}
- Distributed over hundreds of GPUs, with a gradient end to end
- Validated against an independent $N$-body code: about 10 % to $\ell \approx 250$
- A first maximum a posteriori of the initial field from DES Y3-like maps, at the coherence of the Wiener filter ([preliminary]{.kw})

This work is part of a paper in preparation, to be submitted to [JCAP]{.kw}
:::
::::

::::: {.fragment .frosted-panel style="margin-top: 0.6em; --panel-pad: 14px 22px;"}
:::: {.columns style="display: flex; align-items: center;"}
::: {.column style="width: 50%; font-size: 0.9em;"}
[Next]{.kw2 style="font-weight: 700;"}

- the first survey-scale [posterior]{.kw}, with coverage tests
- a better gravity solver: a [learned force correction]{.kw} or a differentiable [moving mesh]{.kw}
- [intrinsic alignments]{.kw} and photometric-redshift errors as latent variables
- [baryonification]{.kw} inside the model
:::

## Drift on the lightcone {visibility="uncounted"}

:::: {.row .bare style="--gap: 14px; --justify: center; --align: flex-end; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
::: {style="width: 285px; flex: none; text-align: center;"}
[10 shells, one redshift per shell]{.kw style="display: block; font-size: 0.6em;"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/14_drift/drift_a10.png){width="285px" style="margin: 0;"}
:::

::: {style="width: 285px; flex: none; text-align: center;"}
[10 shells, drifted]{.kw style="display: block; font-size: 0.6em;"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/14_drift/drift_smooth.png){width="285px" style="margin: 0;"}
:::

::: {style="width: 285px; flex: none; text-align: center;"}
[40 shells, one redshift per shell]{.kw style="display: block; font-size: 0.6em;"}

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/14_drift/drift_a40.png){width="285px" style="margin: 0;"}
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/14_drift/drift_cbar.svg){style="height: 260px; flex: none; margin: 0 0 6px;"}
::::

:::: {style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #25406b; --eq-size: 0.9em; --eq-math-margin: 0.2em 0; margin: 0 auto; width: fit-content;"}
$$a_{\mathrm{c}} = a\big(\chi = \lVert \mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{obs}} \rVert\big), \qquad \mathbf{x}(a_{\mathrm{c}}) = \mathbf{x}(a_i) + \boldsymbol{\pi}\,\big[D(a_{\mathrm{c}}) - D(a_i)\big]$$
:::

[$a_i$: scale factor of the shell, $a_{\mathrm{c}}$: scale factor at which the particle crosses the lightcone, $\boldsymbol{\pi} = \mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}/\mathrm{d}D$: BullFrog momentum]{.caption style="--cap-size: 0.6em; margin-top: 0.3em;"}
::::

:::: {.solutionbox style="margin-top: 0.3em;"}
::: {.solutionbox-header style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
Interpolating the particles onto the observer's lightcone
:::

::: {.solutionbox-body style="font-size: 0.8em;"}
Each particle is drifted to the scale factor at which it [crosses the lightcone]{.kw}
:::
::::

::: {.grid .bare style="--cols: 430px 1fr; --gap: 20px; --align: center; margin-top: 0.4em;"}
::: {.eqbox style="--eq-border: #25406b; --eq-size: 0.68em; --eq-math-margin: 0.3em 0; margin: 0 auto; width: fit-content;"}
$$T_\ell = \begin{cases} 1, & \ell \le \ell_\mathrm{cut} - \ell_\mathrm{width} \\ \tfrac12\left(1 + \cos \pi x\right), & \ell_\mathrm{cut} - \ell_\mathrm{width} < \ell < \ell_\mathrm{cut} \\ 0, & \ell \ge \ell_\mathrm{cut} \end{cases}$$

$$x = \frac{\ell - (\ell_\mathrm{cut} - \ell_\mathrm{width})}{\ell_\mathrm{width}}$$
:::

![](PhD/5_contribution/fli/backup/scalecut_spectra.svg){width="560px"}
:::
